subject: GPU Fleet Projection: prompt-tail profiling & SLA tradeoffs
messages:
From: Alice Smith <alice@acme.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Bob Chen <bob.chen@acme.ai>
Date: Thu, 20 Jul 2028 13:14:00 -0400
Subject: Dedicated capacity planning — quick workload sketch

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the intro earlier this week. Bob and I pulled together a quick sketch of our inference profile and wanted your take before we fill out the formal questionnaire. High level:

- Product: conversational summarization + on-the-fly codegen (internal tooling + paid API tier).
- Peak concurrent users (external-facing API): ~1,200 active concurrent requests during launch day spikes; steady-state active concurrency ~180.
- Request mix: 60% short prompts (<= 120 tokens) -> 40 tokens output on avg, 30% mid (<= 512 tokens), 10% long (1k+ tokens) mostly for multi-turn summarization with 2k token outputs.
- P50 latency target: 90ms; p95: 220ms; p99: 400ms for paid SLA customers. We can tolerate up to 750ms p99 for internal tooling.
- Burst profile: sudden 10–15x spikes for ~5–12 minutes during batch processing windows.
- Auth & privacy: strict customer data residency in us-east; HIPAA-sensitive dataset for some customers.

Attached is a CSV with token distribution and a short CSV of sample traffic traces. Can you give a back-of-envelope for GPU class (A100 vs H100 vs L40) and roughly how many cards we'd need for reserved dedicated capacity? Also, how much headroom should we reserve for cache warming + prompt tail effects?

Appreciate any quick rules of thumb before our call next week.

Best,
Alice
Alice Smith
Director of Platform Engineering, Acme AI Labs
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alice Smith <alice@acme.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_m@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Jul 2028 15:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity planning — quick workload sketch

Hi Alice — thanks for the sketch and the CSV. Quick notes up front, then I attached our compact questionnaire if you want a structured pass:

- Immediate read: given your p99 target of 400ms and the mixed long-tail requests, we should plan for at least two classes: an H100-ish tier for low-latency paid traffic and a quantized/medium tier (e.g., L40 or A10x) for long-run summarization jobs where latency SLOs are looser.
- For the 1,200 concurrent bursts, the right way to size is to convert concurrency -> steady token/sec and then map to per-GPU tokens/sec for the chosen model and quantization. We can do a quick estimate once you confirm model family (open Llama-2-70B variant? custom finetune?).
- Cache warming: allow 20–30% transient headroom for cold-cache spikes and KV cache misses; if you use prefix-caching aggressively, realistic headroom can be 10–15%.

Attached: redwood_questionnaire_compact.pdf (single page) — if you can fill the short answers it cuts the sizing time in half.

I looped in Rishi and Dev for GPU throughput numbers and pricing tradeoffs. Can we do a 30-min call on Monday to review a first-pass projection?

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks — filling the compact version now and attaching the completed PDF and the raw prompt profile (acme_prompt_profile.csv). Quick clarifications we included in the form:
- Model family: we plan to run a fine-tuned Llama-2-70B variant (fp16 for the H100 tier; int8/4-bit quant for the medium tier).
- Avg tokens per request (weighted): 420 tokens in + 520 tokens out for long requests; short requests are ~70 tokens total.
- Typical sequence lengths for cache hits: roughly 1.5 turns (~600 tokens) repeated across cohorts.
- SLA customers represent ~22% of traffic but require the p99 400ms SLA; we want a hard isolation plan for that group.

Files attached: redwood_questionnaire_filled.pdf, acme_prompt_profile.csv

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Alice / Bob — great, thanks for the filled form and profile. Attached is a quick first-pass workbook (fleet_estimate_v1.xlsx) with two scenarios: conservative (heavy headroom + reserved H100 pool sized for 1,200 concurrent p95) and optimized (hybrid H100 + quantized L40 pool with autoscale buffers and traffic shaping). Highlights:

- Baseline assumption: Llama-2-70B fp16 on H100 yields ~2.8k tokens/sec per GPU (sustained throughput with our optimized kernels) for 512-token sequences; quantized path (4-bit) on L40 yields ~1.1k tokens/sec for long sequences.
- For SLA cohort isolation (~22% of peak), we recommend reserving capacity equal to ~30% of H100 pool so that isolation + failover is possible without cross-traffic impact.
- Burst handle: configure burst capacity by configuring a 3x short-term burst credit on the Dedicated pool and a 12-minute autoscale window to absorb short 10–15x spikes. That reduces permanent committed GPUs while satisfying launch-day spikes.
- Cache effects: with prefix/KV caching enabled we modeled a 12% reduction in sustained tokens/sec demand after warm-up; the first 10 minutes of traffic see ~20–25% elevated demand.

Action items:
1) Confirm model artifact (we need the exact HF repo + tokenizer specifics).
2) Approve a quick dry-run spike test on dev Dedicated sandbox (we'll provision temporary capacity for a 20-min run).
3) Slot 30-min sizing review Monday 10:00am PT (I'll send a calendar invite).

Attaching: fleet_estimate_v1.xlsx, short notes inline. If that looks reasonable, we can finalize a recommended reserved SKU mix and an SLO-backed pricing estimate.

Thanks — Marissa
